question: Prediction of MCI progression to AD (pMCI vs sMCI) from structural MRI in ADNI MCI participants. The task, population class and channel (structural MRI) are the same. P-122 feeds a pair of longitudinal scans from two time points, and P-3 a single baseline scan. The brief treats single- vs multi-timepoint input as a matched-figure dimension, so this difference is recorded as a candidate explanation rather than as a different question.
metric: Accuracy with accuracy (84.28% six-fold CV / 84.74% hold-out vs 74.61%); AUC with AUC is also available (0.8599 / 0.8587 vs 0.780).

figures.P-122: Six-fold CV over 823 longitudinal samples from 275 subjects (121 pMCI/154 sMCI): mean accuracy 84.28% (fold SD 1.65), AUC 0.8599 (SD 0.0167). Wilson on subjects (p=0.843, n=275): 0.795-0.881. A fold-based check (84.28 +/- 2.571*1.65/sqrt(6)) gives 82.5-86.0. AUC Hanley-McNeil (n1=121, n0=154): SE 0.024, CI 0.814-0.906. Hold-out test (124 samples; about 41 subjects if 15% of subjects): 84.74%, AUC 0.8587. That headline cannot be squared with its own sensitivity (83.33%) and specificity (82.27%), since accuracy must lie between the two, so the CV figure is used.
figures.P-3: CAAT ensemble, 5-fold CV over 593 subjects (298 sMCI/295 pMCI), one baseline T1 scan each: accuracy 74.61% (fold variance 0.002), Wilson 0.709-0.779 (n=593); AUC 0.780, Hanley-McNeil CI 0.743-0.817.

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. P-122 reports no result from single-timepoint (baseline-only) input; its ablations (71.6%-81.4%) all keep the two-timepoint design. P-3 has no longitudinal input. P-122's comparison table (Table 5) lists other ADNI studies but not P-3. Nothing in either paper places the two results under a shared condition.
performance_validity: Neither study is flagged: 84.3%/84.7% (AUC 0.86) and 74.61% (AUC 0.780) are below 0.97. Both use internal validation only.

candidate_explanations.difference: Two-timepoint longitudinal input (P-122) vs a single baseline scan (P-3). Part of the atrophy trajectory is observed in P-122's input.
candidate_explanations.quote: The architecture synthesizes longitudinal sMRI data from dual temporal points

candidate_explanations.difference: Unit of analysis: accuracy over longitudinal samples (several per subject) with augmentation, vs one prediction per subject.
candidate_explanations.quote: For the sMCI group, we gathered 449 longitudinal samples from 154 subjects diagnosed with sMCI.

candidate_explanations.difference: Input representation: 2D axial slice sequences vs whole 3D volumes.
candidate_explanations.quote: Therefore, we chose the axial section for experimental illustration.

candidate_explanations.difference: Label definition and cohort: DSM-5-guided selection from ADNI 1/GO/2/3 with no stated conversion window, vs conversion within 3 years in ADNI1/2 (Wen et al. splits).
candidate_explanations.quote: Selection of the dataset was guided by DSM-5 criteria, ensuring clinical relevance and rigor.

candidate_explanations.difference: P-3's aim is explicitly single-scan, 3-year prediction.
candidate_explanations.quote: our goal is to take a single MRI image of a patient diagnosed with MCI at a given time and accurately predict whether they will be diagnosed with AD within 3 years.

candidate_explanations.difference: Model selection in P-3 on the evaluation folds. The authors say it biases P-3 upward, which runs against the gap.
candidate_explanations.quote: A limitation of our experimental setup is the use of 5 fold cross validation for both tuning and selecting the models.

reason: Same question (pMCI vs sMCI from structural MRI in ADNI) and same metric. P-122's six-fold CV accuracy (84.28%, Wilson on 275 subjects 0.795-0.881) and P-3's 74.61% (Wilson on 593 subjects 0.709-0.779) lie outside each other's intervals in both directions (two-sample z = 3.4), and the AUCs likewise (0.860 vs 0.780). Neither paper reports a result under the other's condition. The two-timepoint input, sample-level evaluation with several samples per subject, 2D slices and label definition are candidate explanations that neither paper shows to be sufficient. P-122's hold-out headline of 84.74% is internally inconsistent with its sensitivity and specificity, so the judgment rests on its CV figure.
